The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Binance opens crypto withdrawals in phases starting with bitcoin following $6.3 billion hack. Binance reopens customer withdrawals following a record $6.3 billion exploit. Bitcoin leads the first phase. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

FBI confirms North Korea's role in $6 billion Binance hack, asks DeFi community to block BTC, ETH, SOL addresses. While the FBI listed hundreds of addresses in its notice, Chainalysis said the Binance attackers have already used "thousands addresses," and expects this number to continue growing. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin's white paper turns 18, and small businesses are still paying for the bailouts it answered. Eighteen years after Satoshi published the Bitcoin white paper, business owners are still covering the cost of a system built on bailouts, and they can protect part of their surplus by keeping it in bitcoin, argues Onramp CEO Michael Tanguma. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A stolen iPhone, $14,000 in losses and London's crypto theft problem. Two strangers befriended Magnus Ahmad outside a London bar. Hours later, thieves had emptied his crypto wallets, accessed his bank accounts and disabled his laptop. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Traders are already placing leveraged bets on Anthropic’s IPO using crypto contracts. Trade.xyz’s new ANT contract fell about 20% in its first hour on Hyperliquid. There are no shares behind it, and U.S. traders are locked out. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Binance says it has replaced 90% of stolen crypto after massive $6.3 billion breach. Binance is absorbing all losses through corporate funds, futures reserves, and SAFU, keeping user balances intact. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,982 with a +0.74% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,269.57 with a +1.13% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

# Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows

Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows
John Isige

Bitcoin (BTC) is trading above $81,000 on Tuesday, aligning with a lethargic tone in the broader cryptocurrency market. The support range between $80,000-$81,000 reinforces the prevailing stability and consolidation, prompting institutional inflows. [...] Ethereum spot ETFs, on the other hand, recorded $103 million in outflows on Monday, sustaining a four-day bearish streak. Looking back, since September 29, ETH ETFs have posted only one day of inflows, totaling $25 million on October 13. [...] Institutional investors staged a comeback on Monday, with $527 million in Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), up from roughly $82 million in outflows last Friday. Broadly, cumulative inflows stand at $57.4 billion, with net assets under management at $105 billion, according to SoSoValue data. A steady inflow pattern would cushion Bitcoin against headwinds, increasing the odds of a recovery.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Over the years, Bitcoin ETFs have collected a staggering $57.6 billion in net inflows since their inception, whereas Ethereum funds have garnered $13.8 billion. Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024—about six months before Ethereum funds, which debuted in July 2024.

At the current inflow rate, Ethereum funds are outpacing Bitcoin funds by about $525 million annually. However, it would take more than 80 years to close the existing $44 billion gap in total inflows.

items.title: Cryptocurrency regulation: U.S. laws and global developments
items.description: Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it's an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress established a federal framework for stablecoins. Broader regulation of digital asset markets remains unsettled, although Congress and federal regulators have taken steps toward clarifying which assets and activities fall under securities or commodities

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’sGlobal Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. [...] On April 1, 2026, the Treasury issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), seeking public comment related to its implementation of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (the GENIUS Act), a comprehensive framework for the federal regulation of payment stablecoins enacted on July 18, 2025.

items.title: Crypto Regulation in 2026: What Changed and What’s Ahead
items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. items.description:
Stablecoins are moving to the center of global crypto regulation, with 12 G20 economies addressing them through existing or proposed legislation. The US, Canada, Japan, the EU, and the UK are advancing dedicated rules.
